MUQATIL:23:112-116/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:112-116/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:112-116/r3.claim: They stayed only briefly; had they known this they would have acted, but they do not know how long they remained in the graves.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p419#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p419#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p419#2/r4.claim: The time in the world was little compared with the long time they will remain in Hell, as another verse also says.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p420/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p420/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p420/r1.claim: If the disbelievers had been people of knowledge, they would not have entered Hell; other verses contrast their ignorance with the knowledge given to believers.

TAB-FULL:v17p129/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p129/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p129/r1.claim: Most Medinan, Basran, and some Kufan readers take “he said” as a report: God asks the people of Hell how long they stayed, and they say a day or part of one because punishment makes worldly time seem short.

TAB-FULL:v17p129/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p129/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p129/r2.claim: Most Kufan readers instead read an imperative, “say,” reflecting their codex spelling without the alif; other codices have the alif.

TAB-FULL:v17p129/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p129/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p129/r3.claim: The declarative reading is preferable: the surrounding address is plural, so a command would naturally be plural “say”; singular “say” is possible, but declarative singular is more fluent Arabic.

ZAJJAJ:v4p24#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p24#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p24#2/r4.claim: The statement means they remained only a little while.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r5.speaker: ابن كثير في رواية البزي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r5.claim: Al-Bazzī transmits Ibn Kathīr's imperative قل كم لبثتم and indicative قل إن لبثتم, without assimilating the thāʾ in لبثتم.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r6.speaker: قنبل عن النبال عن أصحابه عن ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r6.claim: Qunbul's transmission has قل in both positions without alif.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r7.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r7.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī use the imperative in both positions and assimilate the thāʾ in لبثتم.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r8.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r8.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r8.claim: These readers use the alif form in both positions as indicative statements.

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2512/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2512/r1.speaker: ابن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2512/r1.claim: Their answer that they had lived a day or part of one reflected their own perception.

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2512/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2512/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2512/r2.claim: “You remained only a little” refers to worldly life, which seemed negligible and brief when they saw the Resurrection.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r1.claim: Al-Bazzī's transmission from Ibn Kathīr has an imperative at the question and a reported statement at the answer; Qunbul's cited transmission has imperatives at both places.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r2.speaker: نافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r2.claim: These readers use قال at both locations, presenting both clauses as reports rather than commands.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r3.claim: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read قل at both locations, addressing the questioner with an imperative; the Kufan codex reading قل supports their choice.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r4.claim: These readers assimilate thāʾ into tāʾ because their articulation points are close and both are voiceless; Ibn Kathīr favors clear separation because the articulation points differ.

THALABI:v7p59/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p59/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p59/r7.claim: God says their worldly stay was brief, if only they had known how short it was.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p84/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p84/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p84/r1.claim: Their earthly stay was short: however long the time in the graves, it is finite, and it is short beside their endless stay in Hell.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p84/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p84/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p84/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi explains that anything still to come is near.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p84/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p84/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p84/r3.claim: The phrase if only you knew refers to knowing the length of their stay.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p84/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p84/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p84/r4.claim: Muqatil says that if they had known, they would have understood that their stay was only short.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:114-117/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:114-117/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:114-117/r1.claim: Even if the stay in Hell was long, it is little by comparison; knowing their grave-time would have shown it to be short beside their stay in the Fire.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p432/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p432/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p432/r4.claim: Their stay was little compared with the Hereafter, since worldly and grave residence is finite.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r1.speaker: نافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r1.claim: These readers have qala kam labithtum and qul in labithtum; other readers vary between a command or report for the first verb.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r2.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi use qul for both questions and statements, while al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir has a command for the question and a report for the answer.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r3.claim: The readings mean either God asks and then tells them the stay was brief, an individual is ordered to answer and corrected, or they are questioned before being told the answer.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r9.claim: Their stay is brief relative to torment if it was worldly life, or brief because what is coming is near if it was the grave; ʿabathan means purposelessly, and the two readings of tarjiʿun have the same sense.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p495#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p495#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p495#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p495#2/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p495#2/r2.claim: They read قل إن لبثتم, addressing the questioner.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p495#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p495#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p495#2/r3.claim: The Kufan codices have قل at both places; even a long stay in the world is short beside their endless stay in Hell.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p495#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p495#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p495#2/r4.claim: One reading of if only you knew concerns knowing how long they stayed in the world.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p495#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p495#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p495#2/r5.claim: A second reading is that if they had known they would return to God, they would have acted in preparation.

RAZI-FULL:v23p111/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p111/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p111/r10.claim: “If only you knew” means the stay is brief when one knows of resurrection and gathering; their denial made it seem long.

RAZI-FULL:v23p111/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p111/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p111/r9.claim: Their answer is right insofar as earthly life was brief beside the eternal punishment; the point is to show the shortness of worldly days relative to the afterlife.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:112-114/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:112-114/r8.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:23:112-114/r8.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi also read qal in the clause, while the other readers report it; the stay is short because even a long grave interval is finite and brief beside endless Hell.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:114/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:114/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:114/r1.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read the opening as an imperative, قل, instead of قال.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:114/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:114/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:114/r2.claim: The reply that they stayed only a little validates their answer, adding that they would know this if they understood.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p132#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p132#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p132#6/r1.claim: Their worldly stay was only brief; this is a rebuke for the heedlessness they showed in life.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p132#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p132#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p132#6/r2.claim: The shortened imperative “qul” is read by Ḥamza and ʿAlī.

QASHANI:23:113-114/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:23:113-114/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:23:113-114/r2.claim: They call the stay brief because it has ended; God affirms it was brief, and knowing this would have led them to prepare and detach from its pleasures.

QASHANI:23:113-114/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:23:113-114/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:23:113-114/r3.claim: The plea for forgiveness concerns the forms of attachment, while mercy means the bestowal of perfections.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p588/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p588/r6.speaker: حمزة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p588/r6.claim: The two Kūfan readers make “qul in labithtum” an imperative; the remaining seven read “in” as negation: they stayed only a little compared with their torment, or because whatever is coming is near if the grave is meant.

SAMIN-DURR:23:114/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:114/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:114/r1.claim: لو أنكم has an omitted response: had you known how long you stayed, you would not have answered with such a short span.

SAMIN-DURR:23:114/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:114/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:114/r2.claim: قليلا modifies an omitted time noun or an omitted verbal noun: a short time or a short stay.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p500/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p500/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p500/r3.claim: Whatever the estimate, their life was brief; had they known, they would not have preferred the fleeting world or earned God's anger, and patient worship would have won them the believers' success.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p226/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p226/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p226/r1.claim: Even accepting their estimate, it cannot help them because punishment follows their settled resolve to persist in defiance; God's answer truthfully calls their worldly stay very little, virtually nothing.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p226/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p226/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p226/r2.claim: If they had truly known, they would have preferred lasting reward to transient life and abandoned the frivolity no rational person would choose.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p226/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p226/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p226/r3.claim: Believers should thank God for the joy of their enemies' destruction, inheriting their lands, being honored and blessed with long lives, and continuing happiness in the afterlife.

BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r5.claim: God confirms that the stay was little; grammatically, قليلا describes an omitted stay or period of time.

BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r6.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r6.claim: Al-Bahr says that if they had known how long their worldly stay was, they would have answered differently; the lesson is to repair deeds before breath and life end.

BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r7.speaker: أردشير بن بابك
BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r7.claim: Ardashir says not to rely on the world because it lasts for no one, yet not to abandon it because the afterlife is attained through it.

BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari urges making use of the remaining breath and chance to act, and dropping excuses while one's term is limited.

BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r9.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r9.claim: Saadi's verses urge sowing while it is time, valuing each precious breath, and not wasting one's life in regret because time is a sword.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r1.claim: The speaker is God or an angel; qul is an imperative to the angel as previously.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r2.claim: The two verbs are written without alif in Kufan codices and with alif elsewhere; Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmits this, while al-Zamakhsharī reverses it.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r3.claim: The alif-less spelling may reflect deletion from the past tense contrary to the rule; Qur’anic orthography has other unusual forms.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r4.claim: ‘You remained only a little’ confirms their answer; ‘if you knew’ implies they would recognize worldly brevity and avoid earning eternal punishment.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r5.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ supplies ‘you would not have answered with that duration’; this works only if the prior statement refutes rather than confirms their answer.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r6.claim: Alternatively law is optative and needs no consequence; it should not be a connective particle, since that use without wāw is rare or unattested.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r7.claim: Some exegetes ask about graves because they believed the dead became dust and never rose. Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls it soundest, but al-Ālūsī objects to the inference from the later clause that they would not return to God.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p70#2/r8.claim: A Prophetic report supports asking about worldly residence: after entering Paradise or Hell, people say a day or part of one; the former are praised for mercy, the latter rebuked for fire.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p131/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p131/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p131/r1.claim: The majority keep qāla in the past tense as continued reported dialogue; Ibn Kathīr, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī read the corresponding verb as an imperative.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p132/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p132/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p132/r2.claim: God’s answer requires an implied correction: they stayed for centuries, not a day; compared with God’s reckoning it was still little, as in 2:259 and 22:47.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p132/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p132/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p132/r3.claim: Law makes the knowledge counterfactual: they did not know the stay was little in God’s measure; it was long against their resurrection objection but short beside the torment ahead.

TABATABAI:23:99-118#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:99-118#4/r4.claim: God confirms that their grave stay was brief and wishes they had known in worldly life that they would soon be raised, instead of denying Resurrection and facing endless punishment.

TABATABAI:23:99-118#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#4/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:23:99-118#4/r5.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects treating “if only you knew” as a conditional with an omitted consequence, and finds a concessive reading even less plausible because it lacks a coordinating waw.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p279/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p279/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p279/r1.claim: Rejecters will discover that the respite they thought long passed in a blink; they will then deeply regret their conduct.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r10.claim: Someone among the respondents says earthly life was brief, with rebuke and regret that understanding came too late.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r11.claim: They lived in the world only briefly, but the chance to understand that truth has already passed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r6.claim: The delay in resurrection will soon be exposed as a misconception: what people imagined to be a long earthly life will end like a blink.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p285/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p285/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p285/r1.claim: The dialogue about earthly life occurs among the people themselves, as the parallel exchange in Ṭāhā makes explicit.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p285/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p285/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p285/r2.claim: The dialogue in the Cave sūrah likewise shows people speaking among themselves; it exemplifies awakening from sleep in Barzakh.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p285/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p285/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p285/r3.claim: People assume they will keep living only while alive; after life passes, it becomes a dream of the past.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:112/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:112/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:112/r1.claim: The afterlife dialogue is representative: earthly time is a perception shaped by worldly conditions, and passage into eternal life changes one’s sense of time.

QIRAAT-ER:23:114:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:23:114:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:23:114:1#1/r1.claim: The imperative qul replaces the perfect qāla and changes narrative report to direct command.

STUDYQURAN:23:112/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:112/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:112/r1.claim: The Hereafter makes people view their whole worldly life as no more than a day or hour.

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.claim: The conclusion warns that disbelievers facing their perdition will wish to return to do good instead of evil, but it will be too late.
